chunks: 3. My father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir that `Awn ibn `Abd Allah ibn Mas`ud became sick as I went to visit him. He said: “Shall I not related to you a tradition from `Abd Allah ibn mas`ud?” I replied, “Why not?” He said: `Abd Allah said: “While we were in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (SA), he smiled. So I asked him, “What is it, O Messenger of Allah?” He (SA) replied, “I am surprised at how a believer can worry about being sick. If he knew the reward which resides in illness, he would ask to be ill until he meets his Lord, the Mighty and High.”
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of illness for a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this narration underscores the Shia theological view that illness serves as a mechanism for expiating sins and elevating spiritual rank. The Prophet’s (SAW) astonishment at human anxiety highlights the disparity between perceived suffering and actual divine benefit, encouraging believers to view trials with patience and hope for eternal reward.
